text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: high-rate 429s observed for tenant `emberlane-prod` in VPC `vpc-eu-west-2-12`. 5m error-rate > 45% (HTTP 429). Paging on-call. link: https://alerts.redwood/alert/2376543210

jenny_oncall: oncall here, pulling up dashboards now. pinging CS and platform.

rahul_eng: any recent deploys to dedicated pool handling Emberlane?

jenny_oncall: no user-facing deploys in last 24h. Key symptoms: sudden spike in token usage per request and sustained concurrent streams hitting pool limit. grabbing logs.

jenny_oncall: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T18:00:12Z ERROR tenant=emberlane-prod request_id=abc-123 status=429 reason=RateLimitExceeded model=gptx-13b context_tokens=18240
2026-03-15T18:00:13Z WARN  pool=dedicated-e instance=gpua-07 memory=89% kv_cache_miss=high
```

miho_cs: Emberlane (customer) on the line. Their payments flow is impacted — retries causing downstream failures. They have bespoke contract (SLA + dedicated pool). Customer asks for an emergency lift while you investigate.

sam_platform: proposing two quick mitigations: 1) temporary per-tenant rate override (short TTL) to their committed RPS; 2) reroute their traffic to a separate burst capacity pool `burst-e-1` to isolate impact. prefer doing both to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

rahul_eng: root cause hypothesis: a handful of very long prompts (20k+ tokens) causing KV cache blowout and preventing other requests from getting served — pool saturation rather than pure request rate. Need to limit max_context per-tenant and enable aggressive KV cache eviction for this pool.

jenny_oncall: agree. short-term we can grant an emergency throttle bypass to avoid 429s while we patch routing. Need approval for contract-based override. cc @elaine_sales for sign-off.

elaine_sales: Elaine here — approved to grant a temporary override up to contract limits for up to 2 hours. Please log the reason and expiration, and notify customer. :white_check_mark:

jenny_oncall: executing override now. CLI command: 
```
# grant temporary rate override (admin-run)
redwood admin quota override --tenant emberlane-prod --rps 400 --burst 800 --expires 2026-03-15T20:10:00Z --reason "emergency customer impact: payments failing"
```

jenny_oncall: output:
```
SUCCESS override_id=ovr-0a1b2c created_by=jenny_oncall expires=2026-03-15T20:10:00Z
applied_to_pool=burst-e-1 routing_change=applied
```

deploy-bot: routing rule update applied: `emberlane-prod -> burst-e-1` (version v20260315-3) by jenny_oncall.

miho_cs: Customer confirms immediate drop in 429s, seeing 2xx on retryed flows. They report partial recovery. Thank you.

rahul_eng: monitoring shows 429s drop to <3% within 90s of routing change. I'll open a follow-up ticket to harden pool configs: limit per-req context tokens to 8k for this tenant, add eviction tuning and a fallback to `gptx-8b` for humongous prompts.

rahul_eng: created INC-2026-803 - "Emberlane KV cache saturation causing 429s" assigned to eng-runtime, priority P1. Action items: (1) short-term context cap and eviction (2) add tenant-level quota guard in routing (3) postmortem and customer RCA.

jenny_oncall: leaving override in place until we validate mitigations. Will monitor and let Sales/CS know 15m before expiration.

miho_cs: I'll notify Emberlane that we've applied a temporary routing + quota exception and that we're working on a permanent fix; they want a quick status update in 1h.

elaine_sales: flagged to finance for any billing/contract implications. If override exceeds contract, escalate to me.

rahul_eng: quick mitigations pushed to canary: context cap + eviction policy on `dedicated-e` and `burst-e-1`. Rolling out to 10% now. Logs: 
```
apply config: tenant=emberlane-prod max_context=8192 kv_eviction=aggressive
canary=10% -> success
```

jenny_oncall: monitoring graphs: CPU/mem back to baseline on pool within 12m. No further customer pages.

deploy-bot: override `ovr-0a1b2c` scheduled expiration at 2026-03-15T20:10:00Z. Reminder will be sent 15m prior.

miho_cs: customer requested a signed note that this was an emergency mitigation; creating a support ticket SUP-90531 and cc'ing them.

jenny_oncall: closing pager for now. leaving incident open for follow-up. Postmortem owner: rahul_eng. ETA for RCA draft 48h.

rahul_eng: root cause summary (short): unusual workload pattern — small number of requests with extremely long prompt contexts + lack of tenant context caps allowed a KV cache blowup in dedicated pool leading to head-of-line resource contention and 429s. Fixes: quota guard + fallback + autoscale tuning + monitoring alert rule adjusted to detect per-tenant KV pressure.

miho_cs: Customer acknowledgement: "Thanks for the quick support — payments back to normal. We'll wait for RCA." :thumbsup:

jenny_oncall: will add timeline and logs to INC-2026-803, and schedule postmortem meeting. If anyone needs the CLI runbook snippet I used, ping me.

elaine_sales: thx team. please include any contract-level notes in SUP-90531.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity reduced to Sev-3.

jenny_oncall: signing off from the channel, keep me posted if 429s reappear"
